test.prompt:
Add real-time search with debounce functionality to the following React component. The search should filter the displayed list as the user types, with a 300ms debounce to avoid excessive re-renders. Existing component: ```jsx import React, { useState } from 'react'; const ITEMS = [ { id: 1, name: 'JavaScript Framework Guide', category: 'frontend' }, { id: 2, name: 'Python Data Science Handbook', category: 'data' }, { id: 3, name: 'React Performance Optimization', category: 'frontend' }, { id: 4, name: 'Node.js Backend Architecture', category: 'backend' }, { id: 5, name: 'SQL Query Optimization Techniques', category: 'database' }, { id: 6, name: 'TypeScript Advanced Patterns', category: 'frontend' }, { id: 7, name: 'Docker Container Security', category: 'devops' }, { id: 8, name: 'GraphQL API Design', category: 'backend' }, { id: 9, name: 'CSS Grid Layout Mastery', category: 'frontend' }, { id: 10, name: 'Machine Learning with Python', category: 'data' }, ]; function ResourceList() { return (

Resources

    {ITEMS.map(item => (
  • {item.name} ({item.category})
    • ))}
); } export default ResourceList; ``` Requirements: 1. Add a search input field at the top of the component. 2. Implement debounce with a 300ms delay — do NOT use lodash, implement debounce yourself (custom hook or inline). 3. Filter items by case-insensitive substring match on the `name` field. 4. Show a "Searching..." indicator during the debounce delay. 5. When search input is empty, show all items. 6. Highlight the matching portion of text in each result (wrap matches in tags). 7. Show a "No results found" message when nothing matches. 8. Clean up the debounce timeout on unmount to prevent memory leaks. 9. Handle edge cases: whitespace-only input should be treated as empty, special characters in the query should not cause regex errors. Provide the complete, updated component code.

evalDetails.reasoning: Strong implementation covering nearly all requirements. Debounce is correctly implemented via a value-based custom hook with configurable 300ms delay and proper cleanup on both re-run and unmount (requirements 2, 8 fully met). Search input is controlled and filters in real time using useState (req 1, 5). Case-insensitive substring matching is correct (req 3). useMemo is used for filtered results, appropriately preventing unnecessary re-scans (partial credit on the useCallback/useMemo criterion, though there's no explicit debounce-function memoization since the hook design doesn't need one). Loading indicator ('Searching...') is shown via isSearching derived state, though it's derived by comparing trimmedQuery !== debouncedQuery rather than tracking the actual timer pending state — this is mostly correct but could show 'Searching...' incorrectly in edge cases (e.g., briefly true even when the debounced value will end up equal after trim, though logically fine here). Whitespace-only input is trimmed and treated as empty (req 9). Special characters are handled robustly by avoiding regex entirely and using indexOf, which elegantly avoids ANY regex-crash risk (req 9) — a clean, well-justified design choice. Highlighting is implemented correctly using indexOf-based splitting (req 6). 'No results found' message is present (req 7). Code is syntactically valid, well-structured, idiomatic React with good separation of concerns. Minor deductions: the highlight-matches function only highlights the first occurrence's case exactly as typed but actually loops correctly for multiple matches; no major bugs found. The explanatory notes are thorough and demonstrate clear reasoning, though slightly verbose beyond just code. Overall this is a high-quality, correct, thoughtful solution with only minor nitpicks on the memoization criterion specificity.

The response correctly implements a custom debounce hook using setTimeout/clearTimeout with configurable 300ms delay, proper cleanup on unmount and value changes, controlled search input with real-time filtering, case-insensitive substring matching, useMemo for filtered results, regex escaping for special characters, whitespace-only handling via trim(), highlight matching with <mark> tags, and a 'No results found' message. The 'Searching...' indicator correctly appears during the debounce window (tracking isPending against the immediate query, not just the debounced one). Minor deductions: highlightMatch's split-based approach can mis-highlight if the query appears as a substring of another matched segment in edge cases (though rare given how split/regex capture groups work here, it's actually fine for typical substring matches); the code doesn't memoize highlightMatch or use useCallback for the setQuery handler (though this is minor since useMemo is used for the expensive list computation, which is the main concern). The escapeRegExp and debounce hook are correctly extracted, well-commented with meaningful 'why' comments, and the code is syntactically valid and well-structured. Overall this is a high-quality, thorough implementation meeting all 9 requirements with correct edge case handling.

Strong implementation meeting nearly all requirements. Debounce via custom useDebouncedValue hook with 300ms delay and proper cleanup on unmount (clearTimeout in useEffect cleanup) — satisfies debounce, delay, and cleanup criteria. Search input is controlled with useState and filters in real time via debounced value. Case-insensitive substring matching correctly implemented with toLowerCase().includes(). Special characters handled safely by using indexOf-based matching instead of regex, avoiding crashes entirely (exceeds requirement). Whitespace-only input trimmed via normalizedInput = searchInput.trim(), correctly treated as empty. useMemo used for filteredItems to avoid recomputation; debounce hook itself doesn't need memoization since it's a hook. Loading indicator shown via isSearching flag comparing normalizedInput to debouncedQuery — correctly reflects debounce delay state. Highlighting implemented cleanly with HighlightedText component using indexOf loop, safe and correct. 'No results found' shown appropriately, guarded against showing during active search. Code is well-structured, syntactically valid JSX, uses semantic accessibility attributes (aria-live, label). Minor deduction: the 'isSearching' derived state (normalizedInput !== debouncedQuery) is a clever but slightly indirect way to track searching status rather than an explicit isPending flag, and there's a subtle edge case where if debounced value hasn't caught up but input reverts to match old debouncedQuery, isSearching could be momentarily wrong — minor correctness nuance, not a functional bug in typical usage. Overall a very complete, thoughtful, production-quality solution.

Solid implementation covering nearly all requirements. Debounce is correctly implemented via useEffect+setTimeout (not a custom hook, but inline as the prompt allows), with proper cleanup on both re-trigger and unmount. Search is controlled and filters in real time. Case-insensitive substring matching is correct. Loading indicator shown correctly during debounce. Whitespace-only input handled via trim(), and special regex characters are escaped both for the highlight regex and effectively for filtering (plain includes()). Highlighting via <mark> works correctly using an escaped regex split. useMemo is used for filteredItems, but the debounce/filter logic itself isn't further optimized with useCallback, and highlightMatch is recomputed per item without memoization (minor inefficiency, not incorrect). One correctness nuance: filteredItems is computed from debouncedQuery but the list is hidden entirely while isSearching is true, meaning during every keystroke's 300ms window the previous list disappears and 'Searching...' shows instead of the previous results — this is a UX choice, not a bug, but slightly diverges from typical 'filter list smoothly' expectations. No crash risk on special characters. Code is clean, well-structured, valid JSX with sensible comments (against the constraint of the eval framework, not the model's own instructions). Overall a high-quality, correct, requirement-complete answer with minor missed optimization (useCallback) and a debatable UX nuance.
